test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) launched the SAMVEDNA helpline in 2021 to ______.

options.text: provide guidance to students about career choices
counsel children who witness domestic violence
provide mental support to children affected by Covid-19

solution:
The correct answer is **to provide mental support to children affected by Covid-19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR**) has launched a toll-free helpline called **SAMVEDNA****.**__
 
• To provide psychological first aid and emotional support to children affected by the **COVID-19 pandemic.**
 
• The helpline is trained by** Dr Shekhar Seshadri and his team from NIMHANS.**
 
• The service is offered seven days a week from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. to 8 p.m. at the** toll-free number 1800-121-2830.**
 
• The service is provided to children in three categories: those in quarantine, and **isolation, children with COVID-positive parents, and children who have lost their parents due to the pandemic.**
 
• The service is available in various regional languages such as** Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Oriya, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, etc.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The service was launched in** September 2020** and continues to support children during the difficult times of the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Children need **counselling** now more than ever before.
 
• The Child helpline provides** a much-needed service for children who are struggling with the effects of the pandemic.**
 
• It gives them a place to** voice their fears and ****concerns and** receive support from **trained counsellors.**
 
• The service is available in multiple languages, making it accessible to children from all over India.
 
• **The helpline has already helped countless kids through this tough time** and will continue to do so as long as the pandemic continues.
